pubmed_title: Mutant WD-repeat protein in triple-A syndrome.
phenotype_in_paper: Triple-A (Allgrove) syndrome: ACTH-resistant adrenal insufficiency, achalasia, alacrima, with autonomic and late-onset neurological features incl. peripheral neuropathy
evidence: late-onset progressive neurological symptoms (including cerebellar ataxia, peripheral neuropathy and mild dementia)... identified a novel gene (AAAS)... mutant in affected individuals
earlier_check_query: (AAAS[tiab] OR "triple A syndrome"[tiab] OR ALADIN[tiab]) AND (mutation*[tiab] OR gene[tiab]), pdat 1900-2002
notes: Gene-discovery paper; PN is a recognised core neurological feature of triple-A. Independent simultaneous discovery: Handschug et al. Hum Mol Genet 2001 Feb 1 (PMID 11159947), later date. Earlier hits only linkage/mapping.

pubmed_title: A major determinant for binding and aminoacylation of tRNA(Ala) in cytoplasmic Alanyl-tRNA synthetase is mutated in dominant axonal Charcot-Marie-Tooth disease.
phenotype_in_paper: Dominant axonal CMT (CMT2N), 2 families, p.Arg329His
evidence: Patients present with sensory-motor distal degeneration secondary to predominant axonal neuropathy
earlier_check_query: (AARS[tiab] OR AARS1[tiab] OR "alanyl-tRNA synthetase"[tiab]) AND (neuropathy OR Charcot-Marie-Tooth) -- all hits sorted by date; nothing earlier
notes: Epub 2009 Dec 31. Later: Lin 2011 Taiwan cohort, McLaughlin 2012 Hum Mutat, Zhao 2012 dHMN.

pubmed_title: Tangier disease is caused by mutations in the gene encoding ATP-binding cassette transporter 1.
phenotype_in_paper: Tangier disease (HDL deficiency, hepatosplenomegaly, peripheral neuropathy)
evidence: characterized in the homozygous state by the absence of HDL-cholesterol (HDL-C) from plasma, hepatosplenomegaly, peripheral neuropathy ... Our findings indicate that defects in ABC1 ... are the cause of TD.
earlier_check_query: (ABCA1 OR ABC1) AND (Tangier) AND (mutation*) -- oldest hits; no gene-level human mutation paper before Aug 1999
notes: Three back-to-back papers in the same Nat Genet issue (1999 Aug;22(4)): Brooks-Wilson PMID 10431236 (pp336-45), Bodzioch PMID 10431237 (pp347-51), Rust PMID 10431238 (pp352-5). Identical PubMed date; Rust chosen because its abstract explicitly names peripheral neuropathy as a TD feature. Year 1999 unambiguous. Neuropathy is a recognised core feature of Tangier disease.

pubmed_title: Putative X-linked adrenoleukodystrophy gene shares unexpected homology with ABC transporters.
phenotype_in_paper: X-linked adrenoleukodystrophy incl. adrenomyeloneuropathy (AMN); ABCD1 partial deletions in 6/85 ALD patients
evidence: Adrenoleukodystrophy (ALD) is an X-linked disease affecting 1/20,000 males either as cerebral ALD in childhood or as adrenomyeloneuropathy (AMN) in adults... we use positional cloning to identify a gene partially deleted in 6 of 85 independent patients with ALD.
earlier_check_query: adrenoleukodystrophy AND 1993:1994[dp]; ABCD1[tiab] OR ALDP[tiab] OR (adrenoleukodystrophy AND gene AND mutation*) maxdate 1996
notes: Gene-discovery paper for X-ALD; PN qualifies via AMN (myeloneuropathy) being a recognised core form, but PN is not explicitly documented in this abstract. Sack & Morrell 1993 (PMID 8466536, BBRC Mar 1993) reported overlapping Xq28 deletions without identifying the gene. Cartier 1993 (7904210) gave the first missense mutation. Could alternatively be categorised HSP (AMN = spastic paraparesis + neuropathy).

pubmed_title: Mutations in ABHD12 cause the neurodegenerative disease PHARC: An inborn error of endocannabinoid metabolism.
phenotype_in_paper: PHARC: polyneuropathy (demyelinating sensorimotor), hearing loss, ataxia, retinitis pigmentosa, cataract
evidence: involvement of both the central and peripheral nervous systems, including demyelinating sensorimotor polyneuropathy and cerebellar ataxia. ... we report that mutations in the ABHD12 gene cause PHARC disease
earlier_check_query: (ABHD12 OR C20orf22 OR PHARC OR "polyneuropathy, hearing loss, ataxia, retinitis pigmentosa") maxdate 2010; (ABHD12[tiab] OR C20orf22[tiab] OR BEM46L2[tiab]) AND (mutation* OR variant*) maxdate 2012
notes: Gene-discovery paper; no earlier human ABHD12 variant reports. Earlier linkage paper (mapping to chr20) excluded.

pubmed_title: Pitfall in metabolic screening in a patient with fatal peroxisomal beta-oxidation defect.
phenotype_in_paper: Peroxisomal acyl-CoA oxidase (ACOX1) deficiency (pseudo-neonatal ALD) with polymicrogyria, psychomotor retardation, deafness, retinopathy, peripheral neuropathy, seizures
evidence: The patient presented with ... progressive psychomotor retardation, deafness, retinopathy, peripheral neuropathy, and infantile seizures ... revealed a homozygous acceptor splice site mutation IVS3-1G>A in the ACOX1 gene
earlier_check_query: (ACOX1 OR "acyl-CoA oxidase" OR "pseudoneonatal adrenoleukodystrophy") AND (mutation* OR deletion OR variant*) AND (patient* OR deficiency), maxdate 2006; plus ("acyl-CoA oxidase deficiency" OR ACOX1 ...) AND (neuropath* OR nerve OR peripheral), maxdate 2020
notes: Earlier ACOX1 variant reports (Fournier 1994 JCI PMID 8040306 large deletion; Suzuki 2002 J Pediatr PMID 11815777 missense) do not mention neuropathy in abstracts; PN is not a recognised core feature of pseudo-NALD, so the first paper documenting PN with an ACOX1 variant is chosen. Full texts of the 1994/2002 papers not checked (not in PMC). The dominant gain-of-function Mitchell syndrome (p.N237S, AD, demyelinating neuropathy) was reported later: Chung et al. 2020 Neuron PMID 32169171 (panelapp lead). If the label should reflect the PN-defining Mitchell syndrome, use 32169171 (2020).

pubmed_title: Mutant adenosine deaminase 2 in a polyarteritis nodosa vasculopathy.
journal: The New England journal of medicine
phenotype_in_paper: Deficiency of ADA2: familial systemic and cutaneous polyarteritis nodosa (necrotizing vasculitis) with recessive CECR1/ADA2 mutations
evidence: In all the families, vasculitis was caused by recessive mutations in CECR1, the gene encoding adenosine deaminase 2 (ADA2)... can cause polyarteritis nodosa vasculopathy
earlier_check_query: (CECR1 OR "adenosine deaminase 2") AND (mutation* OR mutant), maxdate 2014/12 (no human ADA2 mutation report before 6 Mar 2014)
notes: ADA2/CECR1 first reported simultaneously in two NEJM papers on 2014 Mar 6: Zhou et al. PMID 24552284 (early-onset stroke and vasculopathy) and Navon Elkan et al. PMID 24552285 (PAN). Neither abstract mentions neuropathy; Zhou PMC full text (PMC4193683) has no mention of neuropathy. Navon Elkan chosen because systemic PAN (mononeuritis multiplex/peripheral neuropathy is a classic core feature) is the described phenotype, but PN documentation in that paper could not be confirmed from abstract. First abstract explicitly naming polyneuropathy in DADA2 with CECR1 mutation: PMID 31522599 (2019); dedicated PN case series PMID 34210540 (2021). If a strict 'PN explicitly documented' rule is applied, the label could shift to 2019. PN is a minority, vasculitic (acquired-type) feature; consider excluding from inherited-PN back-test.

pubmed_title: Mutations in CNTNAP1 and ADCY6 are responsible for severe arthrogryposis multiplex congenita with axoglial defects.
phenotype_in_paper: Severe arthrogryposis multiplex congenita (lethal congenital contracture syndrome) with absent peripheral nervous system myelin (congenital hypomyelinating neuropathy)
evidence: A homozygous missense mutation in adenylate cyclase 6 gene (ADCY6) was found in another family characterized by a lack of myelin in the peripheral nervous system (PNS)
earlier_check_query: (ADCY6[tiab] OR "adenylate cyclase 6"[tiab] OR AC6[tiab]) AND (mutation* OR variant* OR patient*) AND (neuropath* OR arthrogryposis OR contracture* OR nerve) -- all 5 hits inspected; no earlier human report
notes: Epub 2013 Dec 6. Single family; PNS hypomyelination is the underlying lesion causing AMC, so tier 1 judged (could be argued tier 2 as AMC/LCCS syndrome). Co-reported with CNTNAP1.

pubmed_title: Mutations of GPR126 are responsible for severe arthrogryposis multiplex congenita.
phenotype_in_paper: Lethal arthrogryposis multiplex congenita (LCCS9) with defective peripheral nerve myelination
evidence: the peripheral nerves in affected individuals from one family lack myelin basic protein, suggesting that this disease ... is due to defective myelination of the peripheral axons during fetal development
earlier_check_query: (ADGRG6 OR GPR126) AND (mutation* OR variant* OR patient*) AND (neuropathy OR myelin* OR arthrogryposis), pdat 1900-2015/06
notes: Only earlier hits are animal (zebrafish/mouse) studies. PN here is a fetal peripheral hypomyelination inferred from nerve pathology rather than a clinically described neuropathy; a later report (PMID 40752141, 2025) describes distal arthrogryposis with patchy neuropathy.

pubmed_title: Biallelic Mutations in ADPRHL2, Encoding ADP-Ribosylhydrolase 3, Lead to a Degenerative Pediatric Stress-Induced Epileptic Ataxia Syndrome.
phenotype_in_paper: Pediatric stress-induced neurodegeneration (CONDSIAS) with brain atrophy, regression, seizures, ataxia; 6 families
evidence: Abstract: 'recessive inactivating mutations in ADPRHL2 in six families ... pediatric-onset neurodegenerative disorder'. PubMed author keywords include 'neuropathy' (PN not stated in abstract text).
earlier_check_query: (ADPRS[tiab] OR ADPRHL2[tiab] OR ARH3[tiab]) AND (mutation* OR variant* OR biallelic) -- no human patient reports before 2018
notes: Ghosh et al. (epub 2018 Aug 9) is the first ADPRS paper; its abstract does not mention neuropathy, but its PubMed keyword list includes 'neuropathy' (full text not accessible to confirm). Danhauser et al. 2018 Nov 1 AJHG (PMID 30401461) explicitly reports 'axonal (sensori-)motor neuropathy' in 12 individuals. If strict abstract-level PN documentation is required, use 30401461. Same year either way.

pubmed_title: Whole-exome sequencing identifies homozygous AFG3L2 mutations in a spastic ataxia-neuropathy syndrome linked to mitochondrial m-AAA proteases.
phenotype_in_paper: Early-onset spastic ataxia-neuropathy syndrome (SPAX5): spasticity, peripheral neuropathy, ptosis, oculomotor apraxia, dystonia, cerebellar atrophy, myoclonic epilepsy
evidence: We report an early onset spastic ataxia-neuropathy syndrome ... characterized clinically by lower extremity spasticity, peripheral neuropathy ... homozygous missense mutation (c.1847G>A; p.Y616C) in AFG3L2
earlier_check_query: AFG3L2 AND (neuropath* OR polyneuropath* OR "nerve conduction") with maxdate 2011/10/12 (only a 2008 mouse paper); also AFG3L2 AND (mutation* OR variant*) oldest hits
notes: Gene first reported for dominant SCA28 (Di Bella et al., Nat Genet 2010 Apr, PMID 20208537; Edener 2010 PMID 20354562); those abstracts describe cerebellar ataxia with no neuropathy, so per protocol the first neuropathy report is used. Medium confidence because full texts of 2010 SCA28 papers were not checked for incidental neuropathy findings.

pubmed_title: Loss of tubulin deglutamylase CCP1 causes infantile-onset neurodegeneration.
phenotype_in_paper: Infantile-onset neurodegeneration with cerebellar atrophy, spinal motor neuron and peripheral nerve degeneration; biallelic AGTPBP1 variants in 13 individuals
evidence: We found biallelic rare and damaging variants in the gene encoding CCP1 in 13 individuals with infantile-onset neurodegeneration... The human disease mainly affected the cerebellum, spinal motor neurons, and peripheral nerves.
earlier_check_query: AGTPBP1 AND 2014:2018[dp]; (AGTPBP1[tiab] OR "cytosolic carboxypeptidase 1"[tiab] OR Nna1[tiab]) AND (human OR patient* OR mutation* OR variant*)
notes: First human AGTPBP1 disease report; earlier literature is pcd mouse only. Sheffer et al. 2019 reported additional families later.

pubmed_title: [Polyradiculoneuropathy in an adult with primitive hyperoxaluria].
phenotype_in_paper: Primary hyperoxaluria type 1 with mixed demyelinating-axonal polyradiculoneuropathy (intraneural/epineurial oxalate deposits)
evidence: The genetic analysis revealed a mutation of the AGT gene. ... Nerve conduction studies and electromyography supported the diagnosis of polyradiculoneuropathy. Pathological studies revealed mixed demyelinating-axonal lesions
earlier_check_query: (AGXT OR "alanine:glyoxylate aminotransferase" OR "alanine-glyoxylate aminotransferase" OR "primary hyperoxaluria" OR oxalosis) AND (neuropathy OR polyneuropathy OR "nerve") (all years, sorted, earliest inspected); (AGXT[tiab] OR "primary hyperoxaluria"[tiab]) AND (mutation*[tiab] OR genotype*[tiab]) AND (neuropath*[tiab] OR ...)
notes: PN is a secondary complication (oxalate deposition, often with ESRD), not a core PH1 feature. Earlier PH1+neuropathy case reports (Br Med J 1975 PMID 48397; J Neurol Sci 1976 PMID 185338; Can J Neurol Sci 1976 PMID 175908; Am J Kidney Dis 1997 PMID 9186083; Brain Pathol 1998 PMID 9546283; Eur J Gastroenterol Hepatol 1998 PMID 9831280) lack AGXT genotyping in abstract (diagnosis by biochemistry/enzyme). Furby 2000 is the earliest abstract stating an AGT gene mutation in a PH1 patient with neuropathy; full texts of earlier papers were not checked. PanelApp PMIDs: 4701948 (Boquist 1973, pre-gene, no abstract) and 25363903 (Berini 2015, no genotype in abstract). Questionable whether AGXT should be in a PN gene set at all.

pubmed_title: Cowchock syndrome is associated with a mutation in apoptosis-inducing factor.
phenotype_in_paper: Cowchock syndrome (CMTX4): X-linked axonal neuropathy with deafness and cognitive impairment
evidence: Cowchock syndrome (CMTX4) is a slowly progressive X-linked recessive disorder with axonal neuropathy, deafness, and cognitive impairment ... identified a missense change c.1478A>T (p.Glu493Val) in AIFM1
earlier_check_query: (AIFM1 OR "apoptosis-inducing factor" OR PDCD8) AND (mutation* OR variant*) AND (patient* OR family OR syndrome OR encephalomyopathy OR neuropathy), maxdate 2013; "Cowchock syndrome" OR CMTX4 OR (AIFM1 AND neuropathy), maxdate 2013
notes: Earlier AIFM1 papers are infantile mitochondrial encephalomyopathy (Ghezzi 2010 AJHG PMID 20362274, R201del) and prenatal ventriculomegaly (Berger 2011 Mol Genet Metab PMID 22019070); neither abstract mentions peripheral neuropathy (full texts not checked; Ghezzi patients had severe encephalomyopathy/muscle involvement). Rinaldi 2012 is the first neuropathy report.

pubmed_title: Hyperammonemia with reduced ornithine, citrulline, arginine and proline: a new inborn error caused by a mutation in the gene encoding delta(1)-pyrroline-5-carboxylate synthase.
phenotype_in_paper: P5CS deficiency: two siblings with progressive neurodegeneration, joint laxity, skin hyperelasticity, cataracts and hyperammonemia; homozygous R84Q
evidence: a newly recognized inborn error due to the deficiency of P5CS in two siblings with progressive neurodegeneration, joint laxity, skin hyperelasticity and bilateral subcapsular cataracts... Both are homozygous for the missense mutation, R84Q
earlier_check_query: (ALDH18A1 OR P5CS OR "pyrroline-5-carboxylate synthetase" OR SPG9) AND (mutation* OR variant* OR deficiency) AND human, maxdate 2016/12, sorted ascending
notes: The 2000 HMG abstract says 'progressive neurodegeneration' but not neuropathy explicitly; the same two sibs are described in detail in Baumgartner et al. 2005 Eur J Pediatr (PMID 15517380, Epub 2004 Oct) which states 'Both developed progressive neurodegeneration and peripheral neuropathy'. If PN must be documented in the discovery paper itself, use 15517380 (2005). HSP (SPG9A/9B, with motor neuropathy in some) first reported by Coutelier et al. 2015 Brain PMID 26026163. Inheritance: AR (P5CS deficiency, SPG9B) and AD (SPG9A).

pubmed_title: Mutations in the gene encoding peroxisomal alpha-methylacyl-CoA racemase cause adult-onset sensory motor neuropathy.
phenotype_in_paper: AMACR deficiency: adult-onset sensory motor neuropathy (one with pigmentary retinopathy, one with UMN signs), elevated pristanic acid
evidence: Mutations in the gene encoding peroxisomal alpha-methylacyl-CoA racemase cause adult-onset sensory motor neuropathy
earlier_check_query: (AMACR[tiab] OR "methylacyl-CoA racemase"[tiab] OR "methylacyl CoA racemase"[tiab]) AND (deficien* OR mutation* OR patient*), maxdate 2001
notes: First human AMACR deficiency report overall (Ferdinandusse et al. 2000); neuropathy is the presenting phenotype in 2/3 patients. Tier 1 vs 2 debatable (peroxisomal metabolic disorder).

pubmed_title: Disruption of AP1S1, causing a novel neurocutaneous syndrome, perturbs development of the skin and spinal cord.
phenotype_in_paper: MEDNIK syndrome: mental retardation, enteropathy, deafness, peripheral neuropathy, ichthyosis, keratodermia
evidence: founder splice mutation ... found in four families with a unique syndrome characterized by mental retardation, enteropathy, deafness, peripheral neuropathy, ichthyosis, and keratodermia (MEDNIK)
earlier_check_query: (AP1S1 OR MEDNIK OR "sigma1A"), pdat 1900-2009
notes: Explicitly 'the first mutation in the human AP1S1 gene'. Earlier hits are only a 2005 linkage mapping of atypical EKV to 7q22 (no gene).

pubmed_title: Loss of AP-5 results in accumulation of aberrant endolysosomes: defining a new type of lysosomal storage disease.
phenotype_in_paper: Complicated HSP (SPG48) with neuropathy, parkinsonism and/or cognitive impairment; fibroblasts from 3 patients with nonsense AP5Z1 mutations
evidence: patients harbouring nonsense mutations in AP5Z1 and presenting with spastic paraplegia accompanied by neuropathy, parkinsonism and/or cognitive impairment
earlier_check_query: (AP5Z1 OR SPG48 OR KIAA0415) AND (neuropathy OR axonal OR sensory OR "nerve conduction") plus all AP5Z1/SPG48 hits
notes: Gene discovery Slabicki 2010 PLoS Biol (20613862): PMC full text checked - siblings had spastic paraplegia with urinary incontinence, no neuropathy described. Pensato 2014 Brain (24833714): 2 SPG48 patients with ID/TCC/WML, no neuropathy in abstract (full text not checked). Hirst 2016 Neurol Genet (27606357) gives full clinical description incl. sensory and motor neuropathy.

pubmed_title: Variant apolipoprotein AI as a major constituent of a human hereditary amyloid.
phenotype_in_paper: Familial amyloidotic polyneuropathy type III (Iowa / Van Allen type)
evidence: Amyloid fibrils were isolated from spleen and liver of a patient who died with Familial Amyloidotic Polyneuropathy Type III (Iowa). The major protein constituent ... apolipoprotein AI with an arginine for glycine substitution at position 26.
earlier_check_query: ("apolipoprotein A-I" OR "apolipoprotein AI" OR "apolipoprotein A1" OR APOA1) AND (amyloid*) with maxdate 1990 -- earliest relevant hit is 3142462
notes: 1988 paper identified the Gly26Arg variant at the protein level (amyloid fibril sequencing) in an FAP Iowa patient. The DNA-level mutation (G>C codon 26) with segregation was reported by Nichols et al., Genomics 1990 Oct, PMID 2123470 ('A mutation in apolipoprotein A-I in the Iowa type of familial amyloidotic polyneuropathy'). If a DNA-level variant is required, use 2123470 (1990). Tier 2 because the disease is systemic amyloidosis (renal involvement prominent), though the Iowa kindred was named FAP; tier 1 arguable.

pubmed_title: Early-onset ataxia with ocular motor apraxia and hypoalbuminemia is caused by mutations in a new HIT superfamily gene.
phenotype_in_paper: Early-onset ataxia with oculomotor apraxia and hypoalbuminemia (EAOH/AOA1), FRDA-like with sensory loss and areflexia
evidence: a unique group of patients whose clinical presentations are characterized by autosomal recessive inheritance, early age of onset, FRDA-like clinical presentations and hypoalbuminemia... We have called its product aprataxin; the gene symbol is APTX.
earlier_check_query: (APTX OR aprataxin OR "oculomotor apraxia" OR hypoalbuminemia) AND ataxia AND (mutation* OR gene), maxdate 2002
notes: Simultaneous back-to-back paper Moreira et al. 2001 (PMID 11586300, same issue, same Entrez date 2001-10-05) explicitly states 'AOA1 is also characterized by axonal motor neuropathy'. Chose 11586299 (lower PMID; identical date). Axonal sensorimotor neuropathy is a core AOA1 feature.

pubmed_title: Biallelic variants in ARHGAP19 cause a progressive inherited motor-predominant neuropathy.
phenotype_in_paper: Motor-predominant axonal CMT (CMT2KK)
evidence: we identified 16 recessive variants in the RhoGTPase activating protein 19 gene ... our findings establish ARHGAP19 variants as a cause of inherited neuropathy
earlier_check_query: ARHGAP19 AND (neuropathy OR Charcot-Marie-Tooth OR mutation* OR variant*) (all years); ARHGAP19 (all years)
notes: Only human disease report; no earlier ARHGAP19 patient papers in PubMed.

pubmed_title: Exome sequencing links corticospinal motor neuron disease to common neurodegenerative disorders.
phenotype_in_paper: Complicated HSP (SPG61) with sensory and motor axonal neuropathy and acromutilation (family in large HSP exome cohort)
evidence: Abstract: 'we identified 18 previously unknown putative HSP genes'. Full text (PMC4157572) Table 1: 'ARL6IP1 SPG61 ... family 827 ... c.576_579delAAAC p.K193Ffs36X Frameshift C[omplicated]'; neuropathy detail for SPG61 per OMIM 615685 / PanelApp, not in abstract
earlier_check_query: (ARL6IP1[tiab] OR SPG61[tiab] OR ARL6IP[tiab] OR "spastic paraplegia 61"[tiab]), maxdate 2019 (no human variant report before 2014)
notes: Novarino et al. 2014 is the gene-discovery paper (panelapp lead); neuropathy is a defining feature of SPG61 per OMIM/PanelApp phenotype but is not stated in the abstract. First abstract-level documentation of PN: Nizon et al. 2018 Clin Genet PMID 28471035 ('congenital insensitivity to pain, sensory neuropathy, acromutilation, and spastic paraplegia'). If abstract-level evidence is required use 28471035 (2018).

pubmed_title: Molecular basis of different forms of metachromatic leukodystrophy.
journal: The New England journal of medicine
phenotype_in_paper: Metachromatic leukodystrophy (late-infantile, juvenile, adult) in 68 patients; ARSA alleles I and A
evidence: Metachromatic leukodystrophy is an autosomal recessive inherited lysosomal storage disorder caused by a deficiency of arylsulfatase A... we analyzed arylsulfatase A alleles associated with metachromatic leukodystrophy. Two alleles (termed I and A) were identified
earlier_check_query: (arylsulfatase A OR ARSA OR "metachromatic leukodystrophy") AND (mutation* OR gene OR allele* OR cDNA OR DNA OR substitution), maxdate 1992/06, all hits 1987-1991 inspected
notes: Demyelinating peripheral neuropathy is a recognised core feature of MLD (abstract itself does not name neuropathy). Earlier ARSA molecular papers (1989 cDNA cloning PMID 2562955; 1989 pseudodeficiency allele PMID 2574462; 1990 gene structure PMID 1975241) do not report disease-causing mutations in MLD patients. Follow-ups: 1673291 (adult MLD, May 1991), 1684088 (Dec 1991).

pubmed_title: Spinal muscular atrophy associated with progressive myoclonic epilepsy is caused by mutations in ASAH1.
phenotype_in_paper: Spinal muscular atrophy with progressive myoclonic epilepsy (childhood lower motor neuron degeneration + PME)
evidence: Spinal muscular atrophy associated with progressive myoclonic epilepsy is caused by mutations in ASAH1
earlier_check_query: (ASAH1[tiab] OR "acid ceramidase"[tiab]) AND (mutation* OR variant* OR deficiency) AND (neuropath* OR nerve OR polyneuropath*), maxdate 2012; plus SMA/motor neuron query sorted by date
notes: ASAH1 first linked to Farber disease (Koch et al. 1996) which has no PN as core feature. SMA-PME is a (largely proximal) lower motor neuronopathy rather than classic distal SMA/dHMN, so qualification as PN is borderline. Brain Dev 2012 Jun (21982811) Farber case mentions sibling nerve biopsy only, not neuropathy phenotype.

pubmed_title: Recurrent De Novo and Biallelic Variation of ATAD3A, Encoding a Mitochondrial Membrane Protein, Results in Distinct Neurological Syndromes.
phenotype_in_paper: Harel-Yoon syndrome: developmental delay, hypotonia, optic atrophy, axonal neuropathy, hypertrophic cardiomyopathy
evidence: recurrent de novo ATAD3A c.1582C>T (p.Arg528Trp) variant ... in five unrelated individuals with a core phenotype of global developmental delay, hypotonia, optic atrophy, axonal neuropathy, and hypertrophic cardiomyopathy
earlier_check_query: (ATAD3A) AND (mutation* OR variant* OR patient*), pdat 1900-2016/12
notes: All earlier ATAD3A hits are cancer/cell biology/mouse. De novo dominant-negative and biallelic variants both reported.

pubmed_title: The R495W mutation in SPG3A causes spastic paraplegia associated with axonal neuropathy.
phenotype_in_paper: AD HSP (SPG3A) with axonal neuropathy, Italian family
evidence: We report a new atlastin mutation causing spastic paraplegia in association with axonal neuropathy in an Italian family.
earlier_check_query: (ATL1 OR atlastin OR SPG3A OR SPG3) with maxdate 2005/08 (76 hits); all SPG3A mutation papers 2001-2005 abstracts grepped for neuropathy/sensory/nerve - none
notes: Epub 2005 Mar. Gene discovery Zhao 2001 Nat Genet (11685207) = pure HSP. Durr 2004 Arch Neurol (15596607) mentions decreased vibration sense and wasting but no neuropathy. HSN1D (pure sensory neuropathy) first reported by Guelly 2011 AJHG (21194679) - use that if the study wants a PN-primary phenotype.

pubmed_title: Sensory neuropathy with bone destruction due to a mutation in the membrane-shaping atlastin GTPase 3.
phenotype_in_paper: Hereditary sensory (and autonomic) neuropathy with loss of pain perception and destruction of the pedal skeleton (HSN1F)
evidence: In a family with sensory neuropathy with loss of pain perception and destruction of the pedal skeleton we report a missense mutation ... of atlastin GTPase 3 (ATL3)
earlier_check_query: ATL3 OR "atlastin 3" OR "atlastin-3" OR "atlastin GTPase 3" -- oldest hits; no earlier human ATL3 mutation report
notes: Epub 2014 Jan 22. Confirmatory letter Fischer et al., Brain 2014 Jul, PMID 24736309 (novel missense mutation, HSN1).

pubmed_title: A single ataxia telangiectasia gene with a product similar to PI-3 kinase.
phenotype_in_paper: Ataxia-telangiectasia; ATM mutations in AT patients from all complementation groups
evidence: A gene, ATM, that is mutated in the autosomal recessive disorder ataxia telangiectasia (AT) was identified by positional cloning on chromosome 11q22-23.
earlier_check_query: "ataxia telangiectasia" AND (gene OR mutation*) AND 1995[dp]
notes: Gene-discovery paper; abstract does not mention neuropathy. Qualifies only if PN (progressive sensorimotor axonal neuropathy / anterior horn involvement in older A-T patients) is accepted as a recognised core feature of A-T; this is debatable. First explicit ATM-mutation + PN paper found: Hiel et al., PMID 16864838 (Neurology 2006, 'Distal spinal muscular atrophy as a major feature in adult-onset ataxia telangiectasia'). Curator should decide 1995 vs 2006.

pubmed_title: Novel mutation in ATP13A2 widens the spectrum of Kufor-Rakeb syndrome (PARK9).
phenotype_in_paper: Kufor-Rakeb syndrome (extrapyramidal-pyramidal syndrome, cognitive/psychiatric features); ataxia in two and axonal neuropathy in one of six patients
evidence: six patients from a consanguineous Greenlandic Inuit family, homozygous for a novel frame-shift mutation in exon 22 of ATP13A2 ... Ataxia was seen in two patients and axonal neuropathy in one, features not previously related to KRS.
earlier_check_query: (ATP13A2[tiab] OR PARK9[tiab] OR "Kufor-Rakeb"[tiab]) AND (neuropath*[tiab] OR polyneuropath*[tiab] OR "peripheral nerve"[tiab]) (all years; only reviews before 2011); (ATP13A2 OR PARK9 OR "Kufor-Rakeb") AND (neuropath* OR polyneuropath* OR "spastic paraplegia" OR "nerve conduction" OR axonal)
notes: Gene first reported for Kufor-Rakeb syndrome (Ramirez 2006, no neuropathy). Eiberg 2012 is the earliest abstract documenting axonal neuropathy in an ATP13A2 patient (1 of 6). The first report where PN is a recurring feature is the SPG78 paper, Estrada-Cuzcano et al. Brain 2017 Feb, PMID 28137957 ('Nerve conduction studies revealed involvement of the peripheral motor and sensory nerves'), which is the PanelApp lead. If the label should require PN as a recognised feature rather than an isolated patient, use 28137957 (HSP, tier 2). Earlier KRS papers were not checked in full text.

pubmed_title: Mutations in ATP1A1 Cause Dominant Charcot-Marie-Tooth Type 2.
phenotype_in_paper: Autosomal dominant axonal CMT (CMT2DD)
evidence: we were able to define mutations in ATP1A1, which encodes the alpha1 subunit of the Na+,K+-ATPase, as a cause of autosomal-dominant CMT2
earlier_check_query: (ATP1A1[tiab] OR "Na+/K+-ATPase alpha1"[tiab]) AND (neuropathy OR Charcot-Marie-Tooth OR CMT OR motor neuron* OR spastic), maxdate 2019
notes: No earlier germline ATP1A1 neuropathy report found (earlier ATP1A1 work is somatic aldosterone-producing adenoma / physiology). Later: intermediate CMT (He 2019 Hum Mutat PMID 31373411).

pubmed_title: Missense mutations in the copper transporter gene ATP7A cause X-linked distal hereditary motor neuropathy.
phenotype_in_paper: X-linked distal hereditary motor neuropathy (SMAX3) in two families; ATP7A p.P1386S and p.T994I
evidence: We identified two unique ATP7A missense mutations (p.P1386S and p.T994I) in males with distal motor neuropathy in two families.
earlier_check_query: (ATP7A[tiab] OR "Menkes gene" OR MNK[tiab]) AND (neuropath*[tiab] OR motor[tiab] OR peripheral[tiab]), maxdate 2010/06; also (ATP7A OR MNK OR Menkes OR "occipital horn") AND (neuropath* OR "motor neuron*" OR polyneuropath*) maxdate 2010/12

pubmed_title: Exome sequencing and SNP analysis detect novel compound heterozygosity in fatty acid hydroxylase-associated neurodegeneration.

Gene first reported for leukodystrophy/spastic paraparesis/dystonia (Edvardson et al., AJHG 2008 Nov, PMID 19068277), then SPG35 (Dick et al., Hum Mutat 2010 Apr, PMID 20104589) and NBIA (Kruer et al., Ann Neurol 2010 Nov, PMID 20853438); none of these abstracts mention neuropathy and Pierson explicitly states neuropathy had not been previously associated. If the study counts 'HSP genes' from first HSP report regardless of documented PN, use 19068277 (2008). Neuropathy is not a core feature of SPG35 (mild/occasional).

pubmed_title: Biallelic mutations in the ferredoxin reductase gene cause novel mitochondriopathy with optic atrophy.

AJHG 2017 Oct 5 (PMID 28965846) reported biallelic FDXR in 8 subjects with auditory neuropathy and optic atrophy ('sensorial neuropathies'), but full text shows no peripheral neuropathy (one subject hypopallesthesia with normal EMG) - not counted. Peng et al. HMG (issue 2017 Dec 15) full text (Europe PMC) mentions neuropathy in most patients and recruitment for peripheral neuropathy; Slone et al. 2018 (PMID 30250212) explicitly summarises it as 'mitochondriopathy, peripheral neuropathy, and optic atrophy'. If auditory neuropathy were counted, label would be 28965846 (2017 Oct).

pubmed_title: Mutations in FGD4 encoding the Rho GDP/GTP exchange factor FRABIN cause autosomal recessive Charcot-Marie-Tooth type 4H.

notes: Delague et al. AJHG 2007 Jul (epub 2007 May 15). Simultaneous independent Stendel et al. AJHG 2007 Jul (17564972, epub 2007 May 24). 15744041 (2005) is linkage only.

pubmed_title: BiP inactivation due to loss of the deAMPylation function of FICD causes a motor neuron disease.

pubmed_title: Mutation of FIG4 causes neurodegeneration in the pale tremor mouse and patients with CMT4J.

pubmed_title: Mutations in FLVCR1 cause posterior column ataxia and retinitis pigmentosa.

Alternatives if explicit PN in abstract is required: Shaibani et al., Int J Neurosci 2015 Jan (Epub 2014 May 16), PMID 24628582 (FLVCR1 PCARP proband 'presented with sensory polyneuropathy'); first HSAN report Chiabrando et al., PLoS Genet 2016 Dec 6, PMID 27923065.

pubmed_title: Krabbe disease: isolation and characterization of a full-length cDNA for human galactocerebrosidase.

If a paper documenting neuropathy explicitly is required, a later GALC paper would be needed.

notes: Martin et al. AJHG 2013 Feb 7. Abstract does not mention PN, but PMC full text (PMC3567271): 'axonal neuropathy evidenced at electroneuromyography (ENMG, n = 5) and sural nerve biopsy (n = 3)'. Published simultaneously with Hammer et al. (23332917, same issue/date, ARCA with spasticity), whose full-text table also reports axonal sensory(-motor) neuropathy. Either gives the same date.

pubmed_title: De Novo and Inherited Variants in GBF1 are Associated with Axonal Neuropathy Caused by Golgi Fragmentation.

notes: Phenotype spans dHMN and CMT2 (OMIM CMT2GG); categorized CMT. No earlier human GBF1 disease reports (only virology/GWAS).

pubmed_title: Connexin mutations in X-linked Charcot-Marie-Tooth disease.

PN not mentioned in abstract; qualifies via Fabry's recognised small-fibre neuropathy.

notes: Soong et al. 2013; no earlier GNB4 disease report.

pubmed_title: Isolation and characterization of cardiac amyloid in familial amyloid polyneuropathy type IV (Finnish): relation of the amyloid protein to variant gelsolin.
phenotype_in_paper: Familial amyloid polyneuropathy type IV (Finnish type; gelsolin amyloidosis) - variant Asn-187 gelsolin identified by protein sequencing of cardiac amyloid

J Exp Med 1990 Dec 1 (PMID 2175344, 'autosomal dominant form of familial amyloid polyneuropathy') and Maury et al. FEBS Lett 1990 Dec 10 (PMID 2176164); Ghiso et al. Biochem J 1990 Dec 15 (PMID 2176481). If DNA-level evidence is required use 2175344 (same year). Phenotype: cranial and peripheral neuropathy with corneal lattice dystrophy (Meretoja).

If explicit PN in the paper is required: first is den Boer/Tyni 1997 J Pediatr (9003853, 'One patient had peripheral neuropathy', all G1528C homozygous), and first PN-predominant MTP paper is Ibdah 1998 JCI (9739053, exon 9 HADHA mutations, progressive polyneuropathy). Sims et al. PNAS 1995 Jan (7846063) is later than IJlst.

pubmed_title: Peripheral neuropathy, episodic myoglobinuria, and respiratory failure in deficiency of the mitochondrial trifunctional protein.

evidence: The clones showed a G----C substitution at the 3' splice acceptor site of intron 3... 16 of 21 unrelated Japanese patients were homozygous and 4 were heterozygous for this mutation
earlier_check_query: ("xeroderma pigmentosum" AND ("group A" OR XPA OR XPAC OR "XP-A")) AND (mutation* OR gene OR cDNA OR splic* OR cloning), maxdate 1992/06 (1988-1992 hits inspected)
notes: Satokata et al. PNAS 1990 Dec gives the first defined XPA mutation. One month earlier, Tanaka et al. Nature 1990 Nov 1 (PMID 2234061) cloned XPAC and showed 'abnormality or absence of XPAC messenger RNAs' in group A cell lines (no specific variant) - if that counts, same year. Sensory > motor axonal neuronopathy is a recognised feature of neurological XP-A (e.g. Kanda et al. Brain 1990, PMID 2168777, pathology without genetics), but not stated in the 1990 abstracts.

evidence: SPG15 ... variably associated with mental impairment, pigmented maculopathy, dysarthria, cerebellar signs, and distal amyotrophy, sometimes designated as Kjellin syndrome...
